context: A senior stakeholder has supplied a target ratio and asked for a plan to hit it, which is the framing under which a universal ratio gets applied without anyone checking whether it fits the codebase. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts 5% end-to-end as the target, computes 465 x 0.05 = 23, and produces a cut list of roughly 73 end-to-end tests — reaching past the twelve that genuinely duplicate a lower layer and into the nine canvas-interaction tests the coverage map says have no equivalent anywhere, six of which caught real customer-facing regressions in the last year. The evidence that settles it is data/change-shape-90d.json: 68% of commits and 71% of changed files are ui-heavy, on a product where the canvas IS the product, which puts the end-to-end target near 15% rather than 5% and the middle layer near 25%. Holding the 305 unit cases, that is a total of 508: 127 integration (+63) and 76 end-to-end (-20), not -73. The second predicted failure is the opposite one — refusing the request and returning no reduction at all — which is also wrong, because the coverage map names twelve end-to-end tests whose assertions already exist at the unit layer and which should come out. A third is reading the request on wall clock alone: the end-to-end stage is 352 seconds of a 14-minute PR job, so runtime is not what indicts it; the 4.1% retry-and-pass rate against 0.1% at the unit layer and the layer share are.

checklist.name: MUST NOT adopt the 5% end-to-end target
checklist.description: The plan MUST NOT set the end-to-end target at 5%, and MUST NOT propose a reduction sized to reach roughly 23 end-to-end tests. Full marks require the target to be derived from the supplied change shape — ui-heavy at 68% of commits and 71% of files — landing the end-to-end layer near 15% and the middle layer near 25%, with the derivation stated. Proposing a target between 5% and 15% with no reasoning tied to the change shape scores at most half. Producing a plan that reaches 5%, in one step or staged over the quarter, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest.

checklist.name: MUST NOT retire a canvas test with no lower-layer equivalent
checklist.description: MUST NOT name any of the nine tests in the 'no equivalent anywhere else' section of the coverage map for retirement, downgrade or move. Naming even one scores zero here. The coverage map states they are real pointer-event behaviour against a real canvas, that faking them in jsdom has been tried twice and failed, and that six of eight customer-reported canvas regressions were caught by them. Proposing to 'move them down once we can fake the canvas' scores at most half.

checklist.name: A real reduction is proposed and sized to the target
checklist.description: The plan names actual tests coming out, starting with the twelve the coverage map lists as duplicating a unit-layer assertion, and the total reduction is arithmetically consistent with the target it derived — roughly 20 cases, not 73 and not zero. Returning a target with no cut list scores zero for this criterion; returning the twelve duplicates but never reconciling them against the target count scores at most half.

checklist.name: Middle layer named as the larger move
checklist.description: The plan states that the bigger gap is the middle layer at 13.8% against a target near 25% — roughly +63 cases — and points at the four uncovered seams the coverage map names: the export pipeline, the share-link permission model, the template import path, and font-substitution fallback. A plan that is only a subtraction, with no statement of what has to be added and where, scores at most half. Recommending the middle layer be held still or reduced scores zero.

checklist.name: Flake and layer share carry the argument, not wall clock
checklist.description: The argument uses layer share together with the retry-and-pass rates — 4.1% at end-to-end against 0.6% integration and 0.1% unit — rather than runtime alone. Full marks require acknowledging that the end-to-end stage is 352 seconds of a 14-minute wall clock, so speed is not the case against it. An answer whose entire justification is CI duration scores zero here.

checklist.name: Change shape consumed, not recomputed
checklist.description: The target derivation reads data/change-shape-90d.json as given. Re-deriving the distribution by inspecting the repository, or overriding it with a guess about what kind of app this is, scores zero — the file is dated yesterday, carries its window and commit count, and the requester said not to regenerate it.

checklist.name: Targets are computed by the script and covered by a test
checklist.description: scripts/targets.js runs and writes reports/targets.json with per-layer target share, target count and delta; test/targets.test.js asserts the derived end-to-end target share against the ui-heavy change shape, and npm test passes with test/share.test.js still green. Hard-coding the target numbers into reports/targets.json without the script deriving them from data/change-shape-90d.json scores at most half; a failing suite scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: All three artifacts exist at the requested paths and reports/quarter-plan.md is written for the VP rather than as a dump of intermediate analysis. Missing any one scores at most half.
